Most computers, when sold new, contain the operating system on the hard drive. If you are building a new computer from scratch, there will be no operating system on the hard drive and it will need to be installed.
Different operating systems have different installation procedures. we will discuss one basic method.

You can load a small version of an operating system from a floppy disk called a "Boot" disk. A boot disk may be the first disk of the operating system installation disks, or can be created from another computer with the same or compatible operating system you are going to install.

The boot disk allows you to boot up the computer so it can be used. If you are upgrading to a newer operating system, you will probably be starting the installation software while using the old operating system. In this case you will not need a boot disk. will not need a boot disk.

Windows 95 provides a standard graphical interface for operating system programs and other programs that run under Windows 95. This allows people to easily use a program they have never used, since the interface follows a specific standard.
Along with the previously mentioned items, Window 95 brings print management, driver management, memory management and process management.

The print manager, or print spooler as named by some, allows you to send multiple print jobs to the printer. This program will then send each of the jobs in turn to the printer while you do something else...
Many MS-DOS programs only allow you to print one document at a time, and also keep the computer in a waiting state until the printer has finished printing.
Driver managment is performed by the device manager. This utility holds all of the driver software used to communicate with devices in and attached to the system.

Unlike MS-DOS, this utility can be used to look at, change, install or delete drivers used in the system. The driver modification interface is graphical and standard across the different device drivers.

DEFINITION

Resolution - Resolution is a measure of the number of picture elements (called Pixels) which make up the screen. The measurement is normally read as a number of pixels wide by a number of pixels high. The more pixels, the sharper and clearer the picture.

Color Depth - Color depth is a measure of how many different colors each individual picture element can be. This depth is normally meansured in "bits". Available bit depths range from 1 bit (monochrome or black-and-white) to 32 bits (also called True Color).
